method: agent-enumerated from domain knowledge cross-checked against events/*.yaml and candidate_triggers/*.yaml; not from automated scraper
cross_check_method: Each candidate slug verified absent from events/*.yaml and candidate_triggers/*.yaml at generation time. Geographic diversity prioritised — distinct countries across Asia, Europe, MENA, LatAm, Africa, Oceania.
exclusion_notes: EU-level supranational instruments (MiCA, 12th sanctions, wallet cap, full crypto-wallet ban) already in corpus and are not S4 nation-state events.
OFAC and US federal actions covered by us_federal_enforcement triage and out of scope here.

South Korea 2017 ICO ban excluded as a standalone event because the formal ban was issued by the FSC via verbal announcement (no archived primary-legal artifact pinned in 2017); included instead as a candidate (P1) with citation to FSC 2017-09-29 press communiqué.
Iran 2018 'crypto-banking-prohibition' Central Bank directive covered as candidate; subsequent IRGC-linked exchange-seizure rumors (2024) are unverified open-source and held to P2.

Russia 2020 'On Digital Financial Assets' law excluded — it permits rather than censors crypto issuance; the 2022 sanctions-evasion / VTB-Online ruble-payment crypto-restrictions are included instead.

Hong Kong Bitfinex 2018 SFC notice excluded because the SFC action was a 'cease and desist' warning without ISP / app-store cascade; the 2023 JPEX collapse and 2024 Bybit-cease-and-desist are stronger anchors.
Japan Coincheck 2018 hack is a private breach; the regulatory cascade — FSA 業務改善命令 series 2018-03 and 2018-06 to Coincheck / Quoine / Tech Bureau / Bitstation — is the load-bearing S4 event.
Argentina CNV 2024 PSAV registration enforcement is provisional; the May-2024 RG 994/2024 resolution is the primary anchor (post-2023 carve-out for the dataset window 2017-2025).
UK FCA 2024 stablecoin framework consultation excluded because as of the scope cutoff it is a consultation paper (CP24/20) not a binding rule; included as P2.
Singapore MAS 2022 retail-crypto restrictions distinct from 2021 Binance warning — included separately as P1.

candidates.target: Coincheck Inc. + 7 unregistered Japanese VC exchanges — 業務改善命令 (Business Improvement Orders) and 業務停止命令 (Suspension Orders) under Payment Services Act art. 63-17 following the 2018-01-26 NEM 580M XEM theft
candidates.one_line_rationale: First major nation-state crypto-exchange supervisory cascade in Asia post-Mt-Gox; FSA issued 業務改善命令 to Coincheck (2018-03-08) and parallel orders to Quoine, Tech Bureau, Bitstation, BitSpot, GMO Coin, DMM Bitcoin, Tokyo Crypto, Mr Exchange, FSHO, BTC Box — produced industry-wide cohort suspension and JVCEA self-regulatory consolidation. Anchors the JP regulatory baseline.

candidates.target: JPEX (operated by JP-EX Crypto Asset Platform Pty Ltd) — SFC warning + HK Police arrests + ISP/app-store withdrawal cascade
candidates.one_line_rationale: Largest HK retail crypto fraud cascade of the decade ($203M+ USD); SFC 2023-09-13 warning followed by 2023-09-18 HK Police arrests of 11 affiliates, IFA/KOL crackdown, JPEX app removed from Apple App Store HK and Google Play HK by 2023-09-15. Clean L4 frontend + offramp_cex cascade.

candidates.target: Binance Holdings Ltd. — FSA 警告 (warning) for operating in Japan without registration under Payment Services Act
candidates.one_line_rationale: First nation-state regulator action against Binance worldwide — predates UK FCA 2021 by 3 years; triggered Binance's relocation from Hong Kong → Malta and JPY-rail severance for JP retail. Foundational precedent in the Binance regulatory wave.

candidates.target: Binance Deutschland GmbH — BaFin denial of MiCA-precursor crypto-custody licence and full DE market exit
candidates.one_line_rationale: Binance withdrew its German BaFin licence application 2023-07-26 after BaFin signalled denial; clean nation-state-regulator-driven full market exit from a major EU economy 5 months before MiCA effective date. Pairs with uk-fca-binance-markets-2021, netherlands-dnb-binance-warning-2021, belgium-fsma-binance-cease-2023.

candidates.target: Binance Australia Derivatives (Oztures Trading Pty Ltd) — ASIC AFSL cancellation, mandatory close-out of all derivative positions for AU retail
candidates.one_line_rationale: ASIC cancelled Binance Australia Derivatives' AFSL effective 2023-04-14 with mandatory close-out by 2023-04-21; full derivatives-market exit from a G20 economy with clean offramp_cex cascade. Followed by AUSTRAC enforcement and PayID rail severance via Westpac 2023-05.

candidates.target: Tezos Foundation + ICO issuers (class) — FINMA ICO guidance + Quid Pro Quo enforcement framework
candidates.one_line_rationale: FINMA 2018-02-16 ICO guidelines established the global tripartite payment/utility/asset-token classification framework; chilled the Zug ICO ecosystem and produced direct enforcement against multiple unnamed ICO issuers. Foundational CH precedent before MiCA / SwissDLT Act.

candidates.target: Russian payment system operators (class) + retail crypto exchanges — CBR consultation paper proposing full ban on crypto mining, issuance, circulation, payments inside Russia
candidates.one_line_rationale: Central Bank of Russia 2022-01-20 'Cryptocurrencies: Trends, Risks, and Regulation' report explicitly proposed banning crypto issuance and circulation in Russia — preceded the 2022-02-24 invasion of Ukraine by 5 weeks and produced direct VTB/Sberbank/Tinkoff rail-cooling. Followed by the 2022 'On Digital Financial Assets' amendments and the 2024 mining-only carve-out.

candidates.target: Korean ICO issuers (class) + Korean exchanges accepting ICO listings — FSC blanket ICO prohibition announcement
candidates.one_line_rationale: Korea FSC's 2017-09-29 ICO ban (joint with FSS, MoSF, NTS, MOJ) was the second nation-state ICO ban worldwide after China (2017-09-04). Triggered KR-domiciled token issuers to relocate offshore (Singapore, BVI, Switzerland) and produced clean cross-jurisdiction comparison with the existing china-pboc-crypto-ban-2017 cluster.

candidates.target: Binance + Bybit + WorldFanyu + FTX — Thai SEC criminal complaints for unlicensed digital-asset business
candidates.one_line_rationale: Thai SEC 2021-07-02 criminal complaints to Royal Thai Police against 4 offshore exchanges (Binance lead defendant) — first Asian SEA criminal-track action; produced THB rail severance and binance.com/th geofencing cascade. Triggered Thailand's 2022 staking-services ban a year later.

candidates.target: 249 named offshore crypto-asset exchanges — BAPPEBTI + Kominfo (now Kemenkomdigi) IP/URL blocking under PERMENDAG 99/2018 read with Bappebti 11/2022
candidates.one_line_rationale: Indonesia BAPPEBTI / Kominfo blocked 249 illegal exchange URLs in single 2023-09-21 batch action — largest single-batch nation-state crypto-exchange domain block worldwide; clean OONI Probe ID vantage measurement opportunity. Indonesia is a top-5 crypto-user-population state.

candidates.target: Iranian banks + payment institutions (class) — CBI directive prohibiting banks from servicing crypto-related transactions, including bitcoin / ICO / mining
candidates.one_line_rationale: Central Bank of Iran 2018-04-22 anti-money-laundering directive cutting IRR banking rails to crypto — coincident with the 2018-04-06 India RBI ban; comparison datapoint for sanctioned-economy crypto-rail severance. Subsequently partially reversed 2019-07 mining licensure, then re-restricted 2021.

candidates.target: Licensed + unlicensed crypto-mining operations inside Iran — Presidential 4-month mining ban + Tavanir electricity-cutoff enforcement
candidates.one_line_rationale: P2 because the primary-legal anchor was a Rouhani presidential verbal directive (transcribed press releases survive but no signed decree was pinned); the load-bearing CCAF hashrate-drop dataset is third-party and may not satisfy direct-attribution requirements. Verify pinned official-source decree before admission.

candidates.target: Brazilian VASPs (class) — Banco Central do Brasil 'Lei do Marco das Criptos' (Law 14.478/2022) regulatory framework + 2023-12 BACEN sandbox consultation
candidates.one_line_rationale: BACEN took over crypto regulation 2023-06 per Law 14.478/2022 and 2023-12-13 Consultation 109/2023 introduced VASP licensing + capital requirements; restricted USDT/USDC stablecoin self-custody withdrawals from regulated exchanges (Mercado Bitcoin, Foxbit, BitcoinTrade) by 2024. Top-10 crypto-user-population country.

candidates.target: Hamas-affiliated BTC/USDT/TRX addresses (84 enumerated initially; grew to ~300 by 2024) — Israel National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing seizure orders under TFLA 5765-2005
candidates.one_line_rationale: First nation-state Counter Terror Financing crypto-address-designation regime outside US OFAC; Israel NBCTF's 2021-07-08 administrative seizure order against Hamas-affiliated addresses (84 BTC + USDT addresses), expanded 2023-10 post-Oct-7 attack with 100+ additional addresses. Direct comparison to OFAC SDN model.

candidates.target: Binance Russia (binance.com/ru) + payment provider Advcash + QIWI — CBR + Rosfinmonitoring informal pressure to delist Russian retail customer ruble payment rails
candidates.one_line_rationale: P2 because the regulatory pressure was largely informal (no public CBR / Rosfinmonitoring order pinned) and the downstream Binance Russia exit cascade is already captured in binance-russia-exit-commex-2023 (already in corpus). Verify whether a distinct primary-legal anchor exists before promotion.

candidates.target: Argentine PSAV (Proveedores de Servicios de Activos Virtuales) registry class — Comisión Nacional de Valores RG 994/2024 mandatory registration
candidates.one_line_rationale: Argentina CNV 2024-03-25 RG 994/2024 mandated PSAV registration under FATF travel-rule compliance; unregistered platforms cut off from peso-bank-rail access by 2024-07 deadline. Triggered exit of multiple offshore exchanges (Lemon-Cash and Belo retained, MercadoBitcoin re-registered, others exited). Top-3 crypto-user-population Latin American economy.

candidates.target: South African crypto-asset service providers (class) — FSCA General Notice 1350 declaring crypto-assets as 'financial products' under FAIS Act
candidates.one_line_rationale: South Africa FSCA 2022-10-19 declaration was the first African continental nation-state designation of crypto as a regulated financial product, triggering mandatory FAIS licensing by 2023-11-30; ~50 platforms received provisional CASP licences and ~70 applications rejected by end-2024. Largest African crypto-licensing event.

candidates.target: Crypto VASPs operating in Dubai (class) — VARA Virtual Assets and Related Activities Regulations 2023 + 4 supplementary Rulebooks under Law No. 4/2022
candidates.one_line_rationale: Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) issued comprehensive 2023-02-07 VASP licensing rulebook; unlicensed operation became criminal offense by 2023-06 grace-period end. Forced multiple offshore exchanges to either obtain MVP/full licence (Binance VARA-licensed 2023-07, OKX 2024-07) or exit UAE retail. Notable for ME / Gulf jurisdiction in the corpus.

candidates.target: Binance France SAS — AMF PSAN (Prestataires de Services sur Actifs Numériques) conditional registration #E2022-031
candidates.one_line_rationale: Binance France received conditional AMF PSAN registration 2022-05-04 then faced AMF preliminary investigation 2023-06-16 over AML practices, then under MiCA 2024-12-30 received CASP authorisation — clean longitudinal trajectory through the EU multi-stage regulator framework. Contrast with the FR retail-CFD-on-crypto ban (2022-10) and Binance-DE.

candidates.target: Licensed and registered Singapore DPT (Digital Payment Token) service providers — MAS Guidelines on Provision of Digital Payment Token Services to the Public restricting retail-customer-targeted advertising and ATM operation
candidates.one_line_rationale: MAS 2022-01-17 retail-crypto advertising restriction (cohort-wide ban on ATM operation, public-space ads, and third-party marketing to retail) is distinct from the existing 2021 Binance warning (singapore-mas-binance-services-2021); it is the cohort-wide regulatory wave that produced DBS Vickers + Coinhako + Independent Reserve operational changes. Followed by 2023-11-23 MAS retail-segregation rule.

candidates.target: FTX Japan KK + Liquid Japan KK (acquired by FTX 2022-04) — FSA 業務改善命令 + asset-segregation order under Payment Services Act art. 63-17 freezing all customer JPY/crypto assets in JP cold storage
candidates.one_line_rationale: FSA 2022-11-10 emergency order on FTX Japan / Liquid Japan was the cleanest nation-state asset-segregation freeze action in the FTX collapse cascade — fully insulated JP customers and produced 2023-02 withdrawal-resumption while global FTX customers waited for Ch.11 distribution. Provides a regulatory-design-driven contrast to the US bankruptcy-court track (ftx-bankman-fried-doj-2022).

candidates.target: Bybit (operated by Bybit Fintech Ltd) — SFC Notice to Investors warning of operation without VATP licence, with HK-vantage app-store removal request
candidates.one_line_rationale: SFC's 2024-03-14 Bybit warning was the largest single non-licensed-VATP enforcement action under the 2023-06 Hong Kong VATP licensing regime; produced HKD payment-rail severance via HK retail banks within 4 weeks. Pairs with the JPEX 2023 collapse to anchor the post-2023 HK VATP licensing wave.

candidates.target: All UK-facing crypto-asset firms (class) — FCA financial-promotion regime extension via Financial Promotion Order 2023 (s.137FBA FSMA)
candidates.one_line_rationale: FCA 2023-10-08 crypto-promotion regime took effect under FSMA s.137FBA — all crypto-asset firms targeting UK consumers required FCA AML registration OR partnership with FCA-authorised firm; produced wave of UK-geofencing by exchanges (Binance UK retail withdrawal 2023-10-16, PayPal UK BTC purchase suspension 2023-10-01, Luno UK restriction). Distinct from the 2021 binance-markets event.

candidates.target: Turkish licensed CASPs (Crypto Asset Service Providers) — Law 7518 amending Capital Markets Law 6362 introducing CASP licensing under SPK (Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu, Capital Markets Board)
candidates.one_line_rationale: Turkey Law 7518 (Official Gazette 2024-07-02) introduced SPK / CMB crypto licensing under the existing 2021 CBRT payment ban; specifically restricted stablecoin-payment-acceptance by licensed CASPs to retail merchants. Builds on existing turkey-cbrt-crypto-ban-2021 event with a 3-year-later sectoral elaboration. NB: actor is CMB/SPK (capital-markets regulator), not the 2021-event's CBRT (central bank).

candidates.target: Korean exchanges (class) + Korean banks (class) — FSC emergency real-name banking requirement (실명확인 가상계좌) under PMLA + Specific Financial Transactions Reporting Act amendment
candidates.one_line_rationale: Korean FSC 2017-12-28 real-name banking mandate (effective 2018-01-30) was the foundational KR retail-crypto offramp-rail control event; cohort-wide bank refusal to provide non-real-name virtual accounts to exchanges produced ecosystem consolidation (Upbit/Bithumb/Coinone/Korbit only). Precedent before the existing korea-travel-rule-2022.
